definition.note: A plausible-looking finite total curvature minimal surface (two planes joined by catenoidal necks in the pattern later realized triply periodically) whose period problem admits no solution.

construction.blocked_by: PROVED NOT TO EXIST -- not merely unbuilt.  Weber proved that the proposed finite-total-curvature minimal surface cannot close its periods, so no such surface exists; the record is a negative result, kept so the construction is not attempted again.
construction.resume: Nothing to build.  If the family is ever revisited, note that the same neck configuration DOES exist as a triply periodic surface (see the triply-periodic-horgan record).

provenance.definition: Not transcribed. The record exists to state that the surface is absent and why; a fabricated equation would be worse than a null.
sources: M. Weber, 'The Horgan Surface', minimalsurfaces.blog (local mirror: minsurf/book/.../ch062_the_horgan_surface.md).
M. Weber, 'Non-Existent Surfaces (the section index that lists it as a failed construction)', minimalsurfaces.blog (local mirror: minsurf/book/.../ch061_non_existent_surfaces.md).
M. Weber, 'On the Horgan minimal non-surface', Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 7 (1998) 373-379.
